literal_source_claim: Implicit definability and explicit definability are equivalent.
canonical_claim: Let L be a first-order language, let R be one new finite-arity relation symbol, and let T be a theory in the expanded language L union {R}. If any two models of T carried by the same underlying set and having the same L-reduct interpret R identically, then there is an L-formula phi with the arity of R such that every model of T satisfies, for every tuple x, R(x) iff phi(x).
domain_and_universes: A one-sorted Language.{u,v}, any n : Nat including zero, Expanded L n formed by a language sum with exactly one n-ary relation, structures on each Type w with Nonempty M, and an expanded-language theory T.
quantifiers: expanded language L plus distinguished n-ary relation R
pairs of models of T with identical L-reduct on a common carrier
hypotheses: their reducts to L agree on the same carrier
implicit definability: their interpretations of R agree
conclusion: There exists one parameter-free L-formula phi of arity n which defines R in every model of T.
